column1: # p329: the PROCUREMENT SURFACE, all four regions. This closes the gap intel/market.md declared for FOUR consecutive passes:
#   "this file can place REGULATION by region and cannot place VENDORS by region" (market.md:1447).
# p328 prescribed the fix and named it: "drop `players` -- which ranks legal explainers -- and query the procurement surface instead:
#   national framework agreements, ministry tender portals, and university consortium contracts." That is the query this pass ran. It worked.
# THE METHOD FINDING: the vendor map was the wrong OBJECT. Four passes asked "who are the players in region X" and got market-research SEO and
# law-firm explainers, because that is what the word "players" ranks. A studio does not sell to a region; it sells THROUGH A VEHICLE. The
# procurement vehicle is the actionable object, and unlike a vendor list it is nameable, dated, and has an eligibility rule.
# CONFIDENCE -- READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING ANY ROW: every row below is SEARCH-CHANNEL-ONLY. Not one source host is reachable from this session.
# Tested and all 403-at-CONNECT or 000: find-tender.service.gov.uk, geant.org, ocre-project.eu, nwupc.ac.uk, crescentpurchasing.co.uk,
# irishtimes.com, aasa.org, stotles.com, marketbrief.edweek.org, govtech.com, 791coop.org, createyourrfp.com, govspend.com, oecd.ai, unu.edu, cenia.cl.
# So: NO notice number, contract value, date or eligibility rule below is verified at source. Treat each as a LEAD TO CONFIRM on the buyer's own
# portal before it enters a bid document. The notice IDs are recorded precisely so that confirmation is one lookup, not one search.

column3: Pan-European framework for IaaS/PaaS/SaaS to research+education institutions
column4: Began 2025-02-03, runs to 2030-02; 39 participating countries; routes = direct award, mini-competition, desktop mini-competition
column5: THE route into European universities. An eligible institution can direct-award off it -- no new tender. This is the single most useful procurement fact for an EMEA education engagement.

column2: UK DfE "AI Tutoring Tools for Education"
column3: Preliminary market engagement notice (pre-tender), Department for Education (England)
column4: ~GBP 1.5M ex VAT; estimated contract 2026-06 to 2028-05 with possible extension; Find a Tender notices 014992-2026 and 013464-2026
column5: A named national buyer actively shaping an AI tutoring spec BEFORE tender -- the window where a studio influences requirements. Schools/academy trusts then buy via DfE-reviewed frameworks, so the framework is the real gate.

column4: Published 2026-02; SEND advisory lot explicitly covers AI in education systems (adaptive testing, feedback tools)
column5: An already-open UK vehicle whose scope names AI adaptive testing -- i.e. a live route that does not need a new national tender.

column3: North Western Universities Purchasing Consortium (UK HE)
column4: Listed frameworks are NOT AI-specific; the frameworks page does not mention AI
column5: Recorded as a NEGATIVE, deliberately: a named consortium with no AI vehicle is a gap a studio can point at, not an absence of information.

column3: EUR 160M multi-supplier framework, further education and training services
column4: Collapsed before award over process "anomalies" (reported 2026-03-05); ETBs may use interim LOCAL arrangements until a new national framework exists
column5: A cancelled national framework is a near-term OPENING: interim local buying, smaller lots, less competition, and a national re-run to position for.

column2: EU AI Act national regulatory sandboxes
column3: Art. 57 national sandboxes under the AI Act
column4: Deferred to 2027-08-02 by the Digital Omnibus
column5: The ONLY genuinely new EMEA regulatory date this pass. Everything else the regional sweep returned (Annex III to 2027-12-02, Annex I to 2028-08-02, OJ 2026-07-24, EP 2026-06-16, Council 2026-06-29) this file ALREADY HOLDS, with better precision than the snippets.

column3: One cooperative runs one solicitation and awards; member agencies then buy off that contract without running their own RFP
column4: Named vehicles: Sourcewell, OMNIA Partners, NASPO ValuePoint
column5: THE North America mechanism, and it inverts the sales motion: win ONE cooperative solicitation and become buyable by every member district. This is the regional equivalent of OCRE and this KB had neither name recorded.

column3: RFP 791202603005 "AI Services and Solutions for Government", led by Central Texas Council of Governments
column4: Scope includes school districts; not AI-tutoring-specific
column5: A live, named, AI-scoped cooperative solicitation reaching districts.

column2: California Ed Tech Joint Powers Authority
column4: Solicitation dated 2025-07-28 -- NOTE: 2025, not 2026. Builds a PORTFOLIO of pre-vetted vendors rather than selecting one winner; scope includes tutoring
column5: The pre-vetted-portfolio model is the one to design a bid around: it is not winner-take-all, so a specialist studio can get on the list.

column3: 2026 consulting and instructional resources award, includes an AI vendor
USD 8M RFP for AI tutoring solutions -- NONPROFIT, not a state agency
column5: Recorded with its weakness stated: single secondary source, non-governmental buyer. A lead, not a vehicle.

column2: State education agency AI tutoring RFP
column5: An INFORMED GAP: no 2026 state-level AI-tutoring RFP surfaced. SEA buying concentrates on assessment, data systems, licensure platforms and programme evaluation, and posts to the STATE CENTRAL procurement portal rather than the agency site -- which is where the next pass should look.

column3: Official guidance to Chilean public entities on BUYING data-science and AI projects, via Mercado Publico
column4: 2023 version updated 2026-03, reflecting the reform of Law No. 19,886 and its new regulation
column5: THE most actionable LATAM procurement artefact this KB has found: not a market forecast but the RULEBOOK a Chilean public buyer must follow. Read it and you know the shape of the bid before it is published.

column3: National AI plan with goals to 2028, including AI literacy in primary and secondary education
column4: Watch MCTI, MEC, federal universities, and the SENAI/SENAC networks
column5: Names the actual institutional buyers behind a national plan this KB already held as policy. Policy to buyer is the step that was missing.

column4: CompraNet federal data reported FROZEN AT 2022, only Nuevo Leon live
column5: A named data defect is worth more than a portal list: Mexico cannot be monitored federally, so Mexican coverage must be state-level or it is fiction.

column3: Regional convening body with a shared roadmap
column4: Roadmap period 2026-2029; partners include CENIA, CETIC.br, Tec de Monterrey (this base also holds Ceibal)
column5: ALREADY HELD by intel/market.md (lines 323, 641, 704) -- recorded here as held, not as new, so the pass does not double-count it.

column2: China MoE "AI Plus Education" action plan
column4: Announced 2026-04-10, runs to 2030; provincial and municipal bureaus EXPECTED to begin AI procurement in 2026-2027
column5: The plan itself is ALREADY HELD (README:1361, README:4190, with hour floors). What is new is the PROCUREMENT read: the buying happens at provincial/municipal level, so the addressable buyer is a province, not the ministry.
column6: search-channel-only; the 2026-2027 procurement timing is an EXPECTATION, not a confirmed tender

column5: An INFORMED GAP: no APAC framework agreement or consortium vehicle surfaced. The regional query returned enterprise-AI commentary plus two commercial training alliances (TCS-Pearson; LearnUpon Sydney HQ), which are competitor signals, not vehicles.
